page: The Microsoft Azure M128bds_3_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for memory-dense, data-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processor running at 4.0 GHz, the instance delivers 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware-assisted capabilities include Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets, supported by a 105 MB L3 cache. Memory provisioning reaches 2794.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 21.83 GB per vCPU. The instance integrates 6442 GB of high-speed local SSD storage, operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory and storage throughput. The platform achieves 432.24 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 187.69 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB memory blocks, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded performance is equally strong, logging 110316.39 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 106798.23 on the PassMark CPU suite. In database operational benchmarks, the instance registered 139.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 122.22 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Single-core results on stress-ng and bzip3 decompression occupy the middle tier, confirming that the instance's strengths center on aggregated multi-threaded throughput and memory capacity.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, the M128bds_3_v3 consolidates extreme memory density and expansive local SSD storage into a single host envelope. This consolidation minimizes network latency and eliminates distributed clustering overhead for datasets that fit entirely into system memory. Given the dedicated allocation of 128 vCPUs and massive RAM reserves, the instance serves as a dedicated host for large-scale in-memory relational databases, real-time caching layers, and high-concurrency transactional systems.
description: Microsoft Azure M128bds_3_v3 is a memory-optimized instance built on the Intel Xeon 8473C architecture running at 4.0 GHz. It supplies 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores, 2794.0 GB of system memory, and 6442 GB of bundled local SSD storage, with no discrete GPUs. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance supports AMX and AVX-512 extensions. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show top-tier execution across multi-core computing, delivering 432.24 GB/sec in uncached memory reads, 139.35 million Redis SET operations per second, and exceptional PassMark database ratings. While single-thread benchmarks place in the median range, the platform excels in memory-bound parallel processing. The instance is suited for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale Redis and Memcached deployments, distributed analytical caching, and intensive transactional backends.
